messages:
Sam K: FYI — getting a flood of quota enforcement errors across several orgs since the console change at ~09:12. Gateway logs show `applied_default_burst=0` even for orgs that had custom bursts set.
Maria G: ugh, that was my change to make the default explicit for the new policy UI. I thought I scoped it to the staging flag, but I see `apply_to_children: true` got checked in the form. Investigating now. :grimacing:
Kevin T: can you paste the saved payload from the console audit log?
Maria G: here — audit entry 2026-03-17T09:12:02Z:
```json
{
  "policy_id": "default-burst",
  "scope": "global",
  "apply_to_children": true,
  "default_burst": 0,
  "author": "maria.g"
}
```
Sam K: that explains it. Some of our edge enforcers read the effective policy and enforce burst=0 => a lot of short bursts turning into persistent throttles. Errors look like: `quota_enforcer: drop request: burst_exhausted (org=acme)`
policy-bot: policy-fanout job failed during propagation at 09:13:08Z — error: TypeError: serializer.serialize is not a function (runtime v2)
Maria G: oh, fanout failed after the DB write. console said "propagation queued" but the fanout job errored and never reconciled older replicas. So some edges got the new 0, some kept old; mismatch is worse than a full revert.
Lisa H: quick mitigation — can we force a full fanout and then roll the default back to previous value? Kevin, can you run the internal flush?
Kevin T: running now: `curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL" https://infra.internal/policies/propagate?force=true` — returned 202 Accepted. Watching fanout logs.
deploy-bot: rollback action created: revert/console-default-burst-2026-03-17 by maria.g at 09:24:33Z.
Sam K: after revert we still see some edges returning 429s; probably because the failed fanout left inconsistent caches. What are cache TTLs?
Kevin T: cache TTL for edge policy is 300s but there's an additional sticky in-memory map in the golang enforcer that only refreshes on fanout push. I'll trigger an explicit flush to nodes: `kubectl -n infra exec deploy/policy-enforcer -- /bin/enforcerctl flush --all`
Maria G: doing the UI guardrails PR now to prevent `apply_to_children` from defaulting to true and require a confirm modal. Creating PR #1324.
Lisa H: created a short dashboard to surface mismatched effective vs desired policy per-region: https://console/redwood/dashboards/policy-drift — adding to SRE runbook.
Kevin T: flush finished on 120/125 nodes, requeued remaining 5 for retry. Errors correlated to older enforcers (v2) that need a restart — I'll orchestrate a rolling restart for them.
Sam K: monitoring client error rates — dropping from 45% -> 6% over last 15m after flush + rollback. Still watching.
Maria G: apologies, my mistake. I'll own the postmortem + PR to harden the console UX.
Lisa H: long-term action items: (1) add a pre-propagation dry-run check, (2) make fanout job idempotent and retryable, (3) add a canary propagation window. Adding to backlog and assigning owners.
Kevin T: severity set to P2. Owners: maria.g (root cause + console fix), kevin.t (fanout reliability + node restart), lisa.h (dashboard + runbook).
Sam K: thanks everyone. Please +1 the rollback/flush docs in the incident channel when you update them. :thumbsup:
Maria G: will do — attaching audit link and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1324
policy-bot: policy-fanout job status: FINISHED (successfully propagated to 125 nodes) at 10:05:12Z.
